references.text: Lot warns his family to leave Sodom before judgment comes, just as Moses warns the people to stay away from the wicked men so they are not struck by their punishment.
The prophet calls the people to go out and not touch anything unclean, a similar warning to separate themselves from what is unclean and sinful.
An exhortation to flee from Babylon and not be caught in its sins and punishment, parallel to the warning to stay away from Korah and his followers.
Earlier in the same chapter, the Lord commands Moses and Aaron to separate themselves from the congregation, which prepares for the warning in verse 26.
Again in the same chapter, Moses and Aaron are commanded to keep away from the congregation before God's judgment strikes, a repeated pattern of separation before punishment.
In Revelation, God's people are called to come out of Babylon so they do not share in her sins and plagues, an eschatological parallel to Moses' warning.
Paul quotes the Old Testament and urges believers to go out from among the unbelievers and separate themselves from them, a principle of holy separation.
A warning that the devoted thing will bring destruction if Israel does not remove it from their midst, a similar principle of avoiding others' sin and punishment.
